correctness.rationale: Finite hypergeometric masses obey the displayed monotone likelihood-ratio identity for a balancing move. Quantile coupling of their cardinalities and common random-ordering realization makes the intersection sets nested, preserving inclusion on intersecting with the remaining independent packets. Standard integer majorization transfers complete the proof. Exact mean difference supplies claimed strict expectation boundaries. 6707 exact rational assertions from packaged VERIFY.py stress-test finite instances; infinite statement rests on proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Hypergeometric intersection distributions and mean formulas are classical and are not claimed as contributions. They do not individually assert a stochastic comparison when two arbitrary packet sizes are balanced while all other independent rounds persist. The novel proof derives a likelihood-ratio order for the pair, lifts it by an inclusion coupling of random sets, then uses majorization transfers. An uninspected general theorem on stochastic Schur-concavity of random-set intersections would directly cover this result and would overturn the present originality assessment.

value.rationale: Batch-size planning at fixed exposure budget is a natural discrete coupon-collection problem. The theorem controls all tail probabilities simultaneously—not merely the readily computed mean—and proves globally optimal and worst permitted packet-size profiles for every missing-count threshold. An explicit strict finite example shows a meaningful coverage probability difference; pathwise subset coupling explains the phenomenon beyond special cases.
